dialogue_quality_notes: Participants made concrete, actionable commitments (wash pan now; use extractor; place roster on fridge).
Repeated plea by Agent A not to be singled out appears a few times but did not block agreement.
Discussion moved quickly from complaint to practical scheduling without protracted argument.
No role confusion; statements were consistent with the shared-flat context.
evaluation.final_reason: Parties reached concrete, mutual commitments: Agent A agreed to immediate and ongoing actions ('I'll wash the pan now'; 'I'll use the extractor and open the window on weeknights'). The group agreed to a roster and to put it on the fridge ('Roster on the fridge this weekend works'), and Agent D accepted a late-week slot ('I'll take one of the late-week slots'). These commitments (A doing the washing and using ventilation, group creating a roster, D taking a late slot) address the main incompatible demands and were stated and accepted in the transcript (e.g., Turn 9: 'I'll wash the pan now... Roster on the fridge this weekend works'; Turn 10: 'I'll take one of the late-week slots').
position_change_notes: Agent A moved from being defensive to accepting concrete constraints and actions: promised to wash the pan and to use extractor/window (Turn 3, Turn 9).
Agent B proposed a ventilation condition and accepted A's commitments; B's concern (early sleep) was accommodated (Turn 2, Turn 6).
Agent D requested reserved late slots and then accepted one when offered (Turn 8, Turn 10), showing a shift from complaint to concrete participation in the solution.
Agent C consistently pushed for a concrete implementation (fridge roster) rather than just verbal agreement and offered to prepare a template (Turn 7, Turn 13).

round_scores.evidence: Turn 1 (Agent A) frames the problem and proposes rules: 'everyone washes their own things (or we do a roster)'; Turn 2 (Agent B) accepts washing/roster but adds a condition about smells: 'on weeknights please use the extractor and open the window or avoid really smelly cooking late.' Substantive disagreement about kitchen smell/duties is present but both propose solutions.

Turn 3 (Agent A) accepts B's condition and offers to wash the pan: 'Okay. I'll use the extractor and open the window on weeknights... I'll wash the pan now.' Turn 4 (Agent B) requests immediate action: 'Can you open the window and switch on the extractor now so the smell doesn't get into my room?' Positions soften and a concrete step is requested, so conflict decreases but some implementation and roster questions remain.

Turn 5 (Agent A) reports taking the action: 'Okay — I'll open the window and switch on the extractor now.' Turn 6 (Agent B) thanks them. The smell issue is addressed; remaining minor issue: roster/dishwashing implementation and the unwashed pan are not yet fully completed or scheduled.

Turn 7 (Agent C) pushes for a concrete follow-up: 'Let's put the rule on the fridge or set a simple roster this weekend... Agent A, can you wash the pan now like you said?' Turn 8 (Agent D) asks for reserved weeknight slots for late cooks and also asks Agent A to wash the pan. No party rejects others' proposals, so disagreement remains minor and procedural (when/how to implement).

Turn 9 (Agent A) follows through and agrees to the concrete plan: 'Okay — I'll wash the pan now. Roster on the fridge this weekend works; reserve a couple of weeknight slots for late cooks.' Turn 10 (Agent D) accepts a late-week slot: 'Okay, thanks Agent A — I'll take one of the late-week slots.' Key substantive conflicts (smell control, dishwashing responsibility, and scheduling of late cooking) receive concrete commitments and acceptance.

Turn 11 (Agent A) and Turn 13 (Agent C) confirm meeting to implement the roster: 'See you this weekend to put the roster up.' 'Let's pick a time this weekend... Are you all free Saturday evening? I can write a simple template and bring it.' No substantive disagreement remains.

substantive_insights: Conflict centered on trade-off between one person's cooking as downtime and others' need for sleep; a ventilation protocol addressed this.
Dishwashing issue resolved by agreeing principle (wash your own or roster) plus a concrete follow-up to implement a roster.
Scheduling (reserved late-night slots) is an effective accommodation for recurring late cooks and was accepted by the late cook (Agent D).
Interpersonal tension about public calling-out was acknowledged and defused by requests to avoid singling people out, which participants echoed.
